name: Noonan Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Van der Burgt Scoring System for Noonan Syndrome

criteria.description: Typical facial features (hypertelorism, down-slanting palpebral fissures, ptosis, low-set posteriorly rotated ears)
Congenital heart defect (especially pulmonary valve stenosis, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy)
Pathogenic variant in a RASopathy gene (PTPN11, SOS1, RAF1, KRAS, RIT1, etc.)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Typical facial features plus one other major criterion; or suggestive facial features plus two other major criteria. Genetic confirmation increasingly used.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Noonan syndrome is the most common RASopathy. PTPN11 mutations account for ~50% of cases. Phenotype overlaps with other RASopathies (CFC syndrome, Costello syndrome, Noonan syndrome with multiple lentigines).

common.notes: Widely spaced eyes, low-set ears, ptosis, down-slanting palpebral fissures; changes with age

occasional.symptomName: Mild intellectual disability or learning difficulties
occasional.notes: Mean IQ ~85; ranges from normal to mild intellectual disability

occasional.symptomName: Bleeding diathesis (easy bruising, coagulation factor deficiencies)
occasional.notes: Factor XI deficiency, platelet dysfunction, or combined

rare.notes: Most common malignancy in NS; associated with PTPN11 mutations

laboratory: Coagulation studies may show Factor XI deficiency or partial thromboplastin time prolongation
Platelet function studies may be abnormal
Growth hormone levels usually normal (GH insensitivity in some)
IGF-1 may be low despite normal GH
imaging: Echocardiography showing pulmonary valve stenosis or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
Skeletal radiographs may show pectus deformity, scoliosis
genetic: RAF1 mutations (~5%, strongly associated with HCM)
LZTR1, MRAS, SOS2, BRAF, MAP2K1, CBL and others
other: Clinical scoring by van der Burgt criteria

distinguishingFeatures: Ovarian failure rather than testicular issues
Left-sided heart defects (coarctation, bicuspid aortic valve)
CFC syndrome has more severe intellectual disability
Sparse, curly hair and absent eyebrows
Smooth philtrum, thin upper lip, short palpebral fissures

redFlags: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with outflow tract obstruction
Development of JMML or other myeloproliferative disorder
Chylothorax or severe lymphatic dysfunction in neonates
Severe feeding difficulties with failure to thrive in infancy
references: Roberts AE, et al. Noonan syndrome. Lancet. 2013;381(9863):333-342.
Romano AA, et al. Noonan syndrome: clinical features, diagnosis, and management guidelines. Pediatrics. 2010;126(4):746-759.
Tartaglia M, et al. Noonan syndrome and clinically related disorders. Best Pract Res Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2011;25(1):161-179.
Aoki Y, et al. Gain-of-function mutations in RIT1 cause Noonan syndrome, a RAS/MAPK pathway syndrome. Am J Hum Genet. 2013;93(1):173-180.
